tasks.title: len in characters
tasks.statement: Python: len(s). Write char_len(s: &str) -> usize — the number of characters (not bytes).

tasks.title: s[0] and s[-1]
tasks.statement: Python: s[0] and s[-1]. Write first_last(s: &str) -> Option<(char, char)>: the first and last letters, or None for an empty string.
tasks.hint: The ? operator returns None if there is no letter.

tasks.title: Character by index
tasks.statement: Python: s[i]. Write char_at(s: &str, i: usize) -> Option<char>.

tasks.title: Slice by characters
tasks.statement: Python: s[a:b] (by characters). Write substr(s: &str, a: usize, b: usize) -> String — the characters with indexes a..b (b is excluded); for bounds outside the string, return whatever exists.

tasks.title: strip
tasks.statement: Python: s.strip(). Write clean(s: &str) -> String: trim whitespace at the edges and make all letters lowercase.

tasks.title: find without -1
tasks.statement: Python: s.find(sub) returns -1 if not found. Write find_py(s: &str, sub: &str) -> i32 with the same behavior, but the position is a character index, not a byte index.
tasks.hint: find gives a byte position; the number of characters before it is s[..i].chars().count().

tasks.title: str.count
tasks.statement: Python: s.count(sub). Write count_sub(s: &str, sub: &str) -> usize: the number of non-overlapping occurrences (sub is not empty).

tasks.title: replace with a limit
tasks.statement: Python: s.replace(a, b, 1). Write replace_first(s: &str, a: &str, b: &str) -> String — replace only the first occurrence.

tasks.title: split
tasks.statement: Python: [p.strip() for p in s.split(',')]. Write split_trim(s: &str) -> Vec<String>.

tasks.title: Key and value
tasks.statement: Python: k, v = line.split('=', 1). Write kv(line: &str) -> Option<(String, String)> using split_once; the key and value have no whitespace at the edges.

tasks.title: Words of a text
tasks.statement: Python: s.split(). Write words(s: &str) -> Vec<&str> using split_whitespace.

tasks.title: join
tasks.statement: Python: ', '.join(words). Write join_comma(words: &[&str]) -> String.

tasks.title: f-string
tasks.statement: Python: f"{name}: {score:>5.1f}". Write line(name: &str, score: f64) -> String: the name, a colon, a space, and the score with one digit after the decimal point, right-aligned in a field of width 5.
tasks.hint: {:>5.1} — width 5, one digit after the point.

tasks.title: title()
tasks.statement: Python: s.title() for words separated by spaces. Write title(s: &str) -> String: each word capitalized, the rest lowercase; words separated by a single space.
tasks.hint: The first letter to uppercase, the rest to lowercase.

tasks.title: startswith and endswith
tasks.statement: Python: s.startswith(('http://', 'https://')). Write is_url(s: &str) -> bool: the string starts with http:// or https://.

tasks.title: isdigit
tasks.statement: Python: s.isdigit(). Write all_digits(s: &str) -> bool: the string is non-empty and consists only of ASCII digits.

tasks.title: Words in reverse order
tasks.statement: Python: ' '.join(s.split()[::-1]). Write reverse_words(s: &str) -> String.

tasks.title: Anagrams
tasks.statement: Python: sorted(a) == sorted(b). Write is_anagram(a: &str, b: &str) -> bool, ignoring case and spaces.
tasks.hint: Normalize both strings: no spaces, lowercase, sorted.

tasks.title: Character frequencies
tasks.statement: Python: Counter(s). Write top_char(s: &str) -> Option<(char, usize)>: the most frequent character and its count; on a tie, the one that appeared earlier. For an empty string, None. Use a Vec of (char, usize) pairs, no HashMap.
tasks.hint: Keep the pairs in a vector; update the one found or add a new one.

tasks.title: Line wrapping
tasks.statement: Write wrap(text: &str, width: usize) -> Vec<String>: split the words into lines so that each line (words separated by a space) is at most width characters long (a word longer than width goes on a line of its own).
tasks.hint: Accumulate the current line in cur and push it to the result when the word does not fit.

tasks.title: Run-length compression
tasks.statement: Write rle(s: &str) -> String: each run of identical characters is replaced by the character and the run length («aaabcc» → «a3b1c2»).
tasks.hint: peekable() lets you peek at the next character.

tasks.title: Decompression
tasks.statement: The inverse task: unrle(s: &str) -> String unpacks the form «a3b1c2» (each letter is followed by the digits of its count) into «aaabcc». Letters are any non-digits.
tasks.hint: Accumulate the digits in num and reset it at a new letter.

tasks.title: from_utf8_lossy
tasks.statement: Write safe_text(b: &[u8]) -> String: turn the bytes into a string, replacing invalid sequences with the character «�» (use String::from_utf8_lossy and to_string).
tasks.hint: from_utf8_lossy returns a Cow; to_string makes a String.

tasks.title: Case-insensitive sorting
tasks.statement: Python: sorted(words, key=str.lower). Write sort_ci(words: &[&str]) -> Vec<String>: the words in alphabetical order ignoring case; on ties, keep the original order (the sort is stable).

tasks.title: Building a long string
tasks.statement: Write numbers(n: u32) -> String: the numbers 1…n separated by commas with no spaces («1,2,3»). Use String::with_capacity and push_str. For n = 0, return an empty string.
tasks.hint: push_str in a loop, with a comma before every number except the first.
